answer: A trellis endorsement system resists fake identities: a newcomer gains no standing until three unrelated established agents each stake part of their own reputation on that newcomer, and endorsers lose standing if the newcomer later cheats. Trust spreads like a ripple, but each hop halves its weight, so one compromised endorser cannot mint an army. A juniper-style slow-growth rule caps endorsements per epoch, and random re-checks prune identities whose endorsers share devices or copied histories. Attackers pay a distinct stake and sponsor set per fake; honest newcomers pay only patience.
